1.explanation: The MultiSelect component renders its toggle as a <button> and, when items are selected, injects the ListBox.Selection component (which itself renders a div with role=“button”) inside that same <button>. This creates a nested interactive element, triggering the error. Fixing it requires changing how/where the clear-selection control (ListBoxSelection) is rendered—either moving it out of the toggle <button> in MultiSelect or restructuring ListBoxSelection so it does not become an interactive descendant of a button.
1.bug_scenario: When one or more items are selected in the MultiSelect dropdown, the clear-selection icon (rendered by ListBoxSelection as a div with role=“button”) is rendered inside the toggle button (a <button> element). This nests an interactive element inside another interactive element, violating the HTML5 requirement that “there must be no interactive content descendant” inside a <button>.

2.explanation: The MultiSelect component (MultiSelect.js) renders its clear-selection UI (ListBox.Selection) inside the main toggle <button>. That clear-selection UI is implemented by the ListBoxSelection component (ListBoxSelection.js), which uses a <div role="button"> for the clear icon and attaches handleOnClick and handleOnKeyDown handlers to it. Embedding any interactive element (even a <div role="button">) inside a <button> creates nested interactive controls, breaking the HTML5 rule and leading to accessibility violations. To fix this, the clear control must be refactored—either moved outside the parent <button> or rendered as a non-interactive element (or a native <button> with correct structure) so that no interactive descendant exists inside the toggle <button>.
2.bug_scenario: In the MultiSelect component, when one or more items are selected, the component’s clear-selection UI renders an interactive element (a <div role="button">) inside the toggle <button> that opens the list. This nesting of interactive content violates the HTML5 spec (“no interactive content descendant” in a <button>), causing accessibility errors and confusing keyboard/screen reader users.
